content.text:
This is unambiguous — the file was created in commit `b463960` with a syntax error (an `if` block floating directly in the anonymous class body, not wrapped in a method), and `dc4ddf0` is the very next commit (same day, ~5 hours later) that fixes it by wrapping the code in the overridden `performHighlight` method.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: b4639602a22a16c7bd671ffd1cc2d1dafabd501d

## Reasoning
(1) I traced the history of `CustomPieChart.java` with `git log --follow`, which showed only two commits ever touched this file: `b463960` (file creation) and `dc4ddf0` (the given bug-fix). I then inspected the diff of `b463960` to see the file's original content.

(2) Commit `b463960` created `CustomPieChart.java` with an anonymous subclass of `PieRadarChartTouchListener` whose body contains a bare `if (h != null && !h.equalTo(mLastHighlighted)) { ... }` block that is not enclosed in any method declaration — it's dangling directly inside the class body. This is invalid Java (a statement cannot appear directly in a class body) and would fail to compile. The fix commit `dc4ddf0` wraps this exact code in `protected void performHighlight(Highlight h, MotionEvent e) { ... }`, which is the correct override needed to actually intercept and suppress the chart's unhighlight behavior (per the class's own doc comment "Override to disable unhighlight function"). Without this override, the code wasn't just non-functional — it was a compile error.

(3) The evidence is the diff itself: `b463960`'s version is missing the method signature entirely (likely an accidental incomplete copy-paste from the original `PieRadarChartTouchListener.performHighlight` implementation), and unused imports (`View`, `ChartTouchListener`, `OnChartGestureListener`) present in `b463960` were cleaned up in `dc4ddf0`, consistent with the fix commit correcting a hastily/incorrectly written initial implementation from the same author on the same day.

I have high confidence in this identification since the file history is short and the causal relationship (creation → same-day fix of an obvious syntax defect) is direct and unambiguous.
